title: Thermistor Open Circuit
shortDescription: The cavity thermistor has an open circuit.
fullDescription:
F1 on a GE microwave indicates the oven temperature sensor is showing an open circuit. The unit typically disables sensor cooking and may refuse to start high-power cycles.

The fault is almost always the thermistor itself or the harness connection to the control board.

fixSteps.title: Unplug and discharge
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and discharge the HV capacitor before any internal work.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the thermistor harness is seated on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor and reassemble.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not trained to discharge the high-voltage capacitor.

title: Thermistor Short Circuit
shortDescription: The cavity thermistor is reading a short.
fullDescription:
F2 is the short-circuit counterpart to F1. The control sees near-zero resistance from the cavity thermistor — typical when the sensor has failed or the harness has pinched against the cavity.

Replace the sensor after verifying the wiring is not pinched.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for pinch points along the harness route.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement thermistor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you cannot find the pinch point or short location.

faq.q: Can I use manual power cycles?
faq.a: Often yes — only sensor features are disabled.

title: Shorted Keypad
shortDescription: The touch keypad has a shorted button.
fullDescription:
F3 appears when the control board sees a continuously closed key. Grease, liquids, and damaged ribbon cables are the common causes.

Clean thoroughly and reseat the keypad ribbon; replace the touch panel if the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Clean keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe thoroughly and let dry.

fixSteps.title: Replace keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Install new touch panel if issue persists.

shortDescription: The ventilation fan is not turning at expected speed.
fullDescription:
F5 is triggered when the vent hood fan tachometer disagrees with the commanded speed. A dirty filter, stuck blade, or failed motor can cause this.

Clean grease filters first and verify the fan spins freely.

fixSteps.title: Clean filters
fixSteps.instruction: Wash grease filters in hot soapy water.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new vent fan motor if needed.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the motor is accessible only by removing the microwave.

title: Line Voltage Error
shortDescription: Incoming line voltage out of range.
fullDescription:
F6 appears when the control senses voltage outside the 108-132 V band. Brownouts, long extension cords, and shared circuit loads are typical causes.

Measure the outlet under load. If voltage is good, a line filter or control board fault is likely.

fixSteps.title: Test outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage while another heavy appliance runs.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if outlet voltage is unstable.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor

fullDescription: PF indicates a power interruption. Reset the clock to clear it. Frequent PF events suggest an intermittent outlet or house wiring problem.

title: Main Control Board Communication Fault
shortDescription: Control board has lost communication with display or relay board.
fullDescription: Error F1-v2 indicates the GE microwave's main control board has lost communication with the user interface or relay board, or has detected an internal self-test failure. The microwave halts to prevent unsafe operation.
symptoms: Display flickers or is partially blank

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 10 minutes to fully discharge the boards, then plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cables
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the capacitor first. Open the control panel and reseat all ribbon cables between the display and main board. Look for bent pins or corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for surge damage
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burnt components, swollen capacitors, or scorch marks on the main board. Any visible damage means board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace the control board
fixSteps.instruction: If the boards do not communicate after reseating, replace the main control board. Match the part number exactly - microwave control boards are firmware-specific.

whenToCallPro: If a hard reset and ribbon cable reseat do not clear the code, hire a professional. Control board replacement on a microwave can be more expensive than a new unit.

faq.q: Is a control board replacement worth it?
faq.a: Boards are $80-$220. On older microwaves the cost may exceed the value of replacing the unit.

faq.q: Can a power strip prevent this?
faq.a: A surge protector reduces the risk but does not eliminate it. Any large power transient can damage the board.

faq.q: Why does my display flicker before the code appears?
faq.a: Loose ribbon cables and failing capacitors on the display board commonly cause flickering before total failure.

title: Touchpad / Keypad Stuck Key Fault
shortDescription: Control detects a stuck or shorted key on the touchpad.
fullDescription: Error F2-v2 on this GE microwave indicates the control board sees one or more keys on the touchpad as continuously pressed. Worn membranes, moisture, or a bad ribbon cable are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 2 minutes to clear a transient stuck-key reading.

fixSteps.title: Clean the keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the touchpad with a soft, slightly damp cloth. Avoid harsh cleaners and standing water.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the capacitor first. Open the control panel and reseat the touchpad ribbon at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace the touchpad or control assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If the code persists, replace the touchpad membrane or the combined touchpad/control assembly per the model's parts diagram.

whenToCallPro: If the touchpad and control are a single sealed assembly, replacement can rival the cost of a new microwave. A pro can confirm whether replacement is economical.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave F2-v2 stuck key touchpad fix

faq.q: Why does moisture cause stuck keys?
faq.a: Steam from cooking can wick behind the keypad and bridge the key contacts, mimicking a continuous press.
If steam is the culprit, addressing ventilation and avoiding splashes around the keypad helps. Worn membranes need replacement.

faq.q: Can I replace just the keypad?
faq.a: On some models yes; on others the keypad is bonded to the control board and only the assembly is sold.

title: Cavity Thermistor / Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Cavity temperature sensor reading is out of range or open circuit.
fullDescription: Error F3-v2 on this GE microwave indicates the cavity (oven) thermistor used for sensor cooking and convection control is reporting an out-of-range value, an open circuit, or a short. This sensor monitors cavity temperature for sensor-cook, popcorn, and convection cycles. The microwave may refuse to start or limit functions until the fault is cleared.

causes.cause: Thermistor wire harness disconnected or damaged
Thermistor element failed open or shorted
Control board sensor input circuit failure
Moisture or grease on sensor connector

symptoms: Sensor cook cycles fail or abort

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the microwave
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 5 minutes to discharge the control board and capacitor, then plug it back in. A transient sensor reading may clear.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the thermistor harness
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the high-voltage capacitor before working inside. Remove the outer wrapper, locate the thermistor mounted on the cavity wall, and check the connector for moisture, grease, or loose pins. Reseat firmly.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the thermistor and measure resistance with a multimeter. At room temperature it should read roughly 50-100k ohms (model dependent). Open or shorted readings confirm a bad sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Order the correct replacement thermistor for your model and install it in the same orientation. Reconnect the harness and reassemble the microwave.

whenToCallPro: Microwaves contain a high-voltage capacitor that can deliver a lethal shock even when unplugged. If you are not trained to discharge it, call a qualified appliance technician.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave F3-v2 thermistor sensor replacement

faq.q: Can I keep using the microwave with F3-v2?
faq.a: Basic timed cooking may still work on some models, but sensor cook and convection functions will be unreliable. Repair the sensor for safe, accurate operation.

faq.q: How much does the thermistor cost?
faq.a: Most cavity thermistors are $15-$50. The repair is mostly labor.

faq.q: Will a power cycle fix it permanently?
faq.a: Only if the fault is a transient glitch or condensation. A failed thermistor will quickly trigger the code again.

title: Humidity / Steam Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Humidity sensor used for sensor cooking is out of range.
fullDescription: Error F4-v2 indicates the humidity (steam) sensor on this GE microwave is reporting values outside the expected range. This sensor detects steam released from food during sensor-cook cycles. A failed sensor or contaminated grille can prevent the microwave from auto-cooking.

causes.cause: Steam vent or sensor grille blocked by grease

symptoms: Sensor cook cycles abort or never end
Microwave reverts to time cook only

fixSteps.title: Clean the steam vent
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the steam vent on the cavity wall and the area around the sensor grille with warm soapy water. Grease and food residue distort sensor readings.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 5 minutes and try a sensor-cook cycle again.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the sensor harness
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the high-voltage capacitor first. Remove the outer wrapper and reseat the humidity sensor harness at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace the humidity sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning and reseating do not clear the code, replace the humidity sensor module. Order the correct part for your model.

affectedModels: Sensor-cook capable countertop and OTR models
whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable discharging the high-voltage capacitor and working inside the microwave, call a professional appliance technician.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave F4-v2 humidity sensor cleaning replacement

faq.q: Why does grease cause this error?
faq.a: Cooking grease coats the sensor element and changes its response curve. The control board sees readings outside the expected range and posts the fault.

faq.q: Can I clean the sensor itself?
faq.a: Wipe only the visible vent grille with a damp cloth. Do not poke into the sensor element - it can be damaged easily.
If you regularly use auto popcorn, reheat, or sensor cook, yes. Otherwise you can keep using time-based cooking.

title: Door Interlock Switch Fault
shortDescription: Door interlock switches do not agree or are stuck.
fullDescription: Error F5-v2 indicates the GE microwave's safety interlock system has detected a mismatch between the primary, secondary, and monitor door switches. These switches must close in a precise sequence when the door shuts. A worn switch, broken latch, or misaligned door triggers this fault and prevents the microwave from running for safety reasons.

causes.cause: Door latch hooks broken or worn
One of the interlock microswitches failed
Wire to switch loose or pinched

symptoms: Microwave will not start when door is closed
Beeping when door is opened or closed

fixSteps.title: Inspect the door and latch
fixSteps.instruction: Open and close the door slowly. The latch hooks should engage with a firm click. Check for cracks, missing tabs, or sagging.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 2 minutes. Re-seat the door and try a short cook cycle.

fixSteps.title: Test interlock switches
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the high-voltage capacitor first. Remove the control panel to access the interlock switches. Use a multimeter to check continuity at each switch with the latch hooks pressed.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed switches or latch
fixSteps.instruction: Replace any switch that does not change state cleanly, or replace the latch board if the hooks are broken. Reassemble and verify the door triggers all switches.

whenToCallPro: The monitor switch is a safety device that will blow the fuse if the others fail. If you are not comfortable discharging the capacitor and testing safety circuits, hire a professional - a stuck-closed monitor switch can be dangerous.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave F5-v2 door switch interlock replacement

faq.q: Why does the microwave have three door switches?
faq.a: Two enable cooking only when the door is fully closed; the third (monitor) is a safety that blows a thermal fuse if the others fail closed while the door is open.

faq.q: Can I bypass the door switches?
faq.a: No. Bypassing them allows microwave radiation to escape and is illegal in most jurisdictions.
Yes. Even a small misalignment can prevent the safety switches from engaging properly. Repair promptly.

title: Magnetron / High-Voltage Circuit Fault
shortDescription: Magnetron, HV diode, capacitor, or transformer fault detected.
fullDescription: Error F6-v2 indicates the GE microwave's high-voltage circuit is drawing abnormal current or has tripped a fault. The magnetron, high-voltage diode, capacitor, or transformer can each cause this code. The microwave will refuse to operate to protect itself and the user.
symptoms: Microwave runs but food does not heat
Loud buzzing or humming when running

fixSteps.title: Stop using the microwave
fixSteps.instruction: If you smell burning or see sparks, unplug the unit immediately and do not use it again until inspected.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and try a 30-second test with a cup of water. If the code returns, the HV circuit needs professional service.

fixSteps.title: Professional HV diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: the high-voltage capacitor stores a lethal charge. A trained technician will discharge the capacitor and test the magnetron, diode, capacitor, and transformer.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the magnetron, diode, capacitor, or transformer based on diagnosis. Many technicians replace the magnetron and diode together because they fail in pairs.

whenToCallPro: Always call a professional. The high-voltage capacitor can deliver a lethal shock even when the microwave is unplugged. Do not attempt this repair without proper training and discharge equipment.

faq.q: Is replacing the magnetron worth it?
faq.a: On a 1-3 year old microwave, yes. On older units the repair cost can approach the price of a new microwave.
Usually yes - the microwave shuts down. But a failing magnetron can occasionally arc, smoke, or trip the breaker, which is why you stop using it immediately when this code appears.

faq.q: How long should a magnetron last?
faq.a: Roughly 2,000 hours of cook time. Running the microwave empty drastically shortens its life.

title: Cooling Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Magnetron cooling fan not running or feedback missing.
fullDescription: Error F7-v2 indicates the GE microwave's cooling fan that pulls air across the magnetron is not running or its tach feedback is missing. Without cooling, the magnetron's thermal cutout will trip, so the control board halts operation.

causes.cause: Wire to fan motor broken or loose
Control board fan driver circuit failed

symptoms: Microwave shuts off after a short run

fixSteps.title: Listen for the fan
fixSteps.instruction: Start a 30-second cook cycle and listen for the fan. If it is silent or making a grinding noise, the fan motor is the most likely cause.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle and check vents
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes. Vacuum the exterior vents to clear lint and dust. Plug back in and retest.

fixSteps.title: Inspect and free the fan blade
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the capacitor first. Remove the outer wrapper, locate the cooling fan, and spin the blade by hand. It should turn freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace the fan motor
fixSteps.instruction: If the blade is seized or noisy, replace the cooling fan motor assembly with the matching part for your model.

whenToCallPro: The fan replacement requires removing the outer wrapper and working near the high-voltage capacitor. If you cannot safely discharge the capacitor, call a professional.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave F7-v2 cooling fan motor replacement

faq.q: Can I keep cooking if the fan is loud?
faq.a: Briefly, but a noisy fan is a sign of bearing failure and will eventually seize. Replace it before it stops the magnetron from cooling.

faq.q: Does the fan run all the time?
faq.a: It runs whenever the magnetron is on, and on many models it continues for a cool-down period after cooking ends.

faq.q: Could a vent block cause this?
faq.a: Yes. Clear external vents above and below the door of any obstructions like cabinets or grease.

title: Turntable Motor Fault
shortDescription: Turntable motor not turning or feedback missing.
fullDescription: Error F8-v2 on this GE microwave indicates the turntable motor is not running. Many models monitor the turntable to ensure even cooking and will post a fault when it stops. A jammed plate, broken coupler, or failed motor are the typical causes.

causes.cause: Turntable coupler or roller ring stuck

symptoms: Grinding sound from base of cavity

fixSteps.title: Clean and reseat the turntable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the glass tray and roller ring. Wash both, wipe out the cavity floor, and reseat the tray squarely on the coupler.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 2 minutes and run a 30-second test cycle. The tray should turn smoothly.

fixSteps.title: Access and test the turntable motor
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: discharge the capacitor first. Remove the bottom panel of the microwave to access the turntable motor. Test motor terminals for resistance with a multimeter - typically 30-50 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Replace the turntable motor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the harness and unscrew the motor from the cavity floor. Install the new motor in the same orientation and reconnect.

affectedModels: Most countertop and OTR models with motorized turntable
whenToCallPro: The turntable motor sits below the cavity and is generally a safer DIY part than HV components, but you still need to discharge the capacitor before opening the case. If you are not sure, hire a technician.

faq.q: Can I run the microwave with no turntable?
faq.a: Most modern models block heating when the turntable fault is active. Some older units allow it but cooking will be uneven.
No. The turntable motor is one of the cheapest microwave parts at $15-$45.

faq.q: Why is the tray not turning even though the motor sounds OK?
faq.a: Check the coupler on top of the motor shaft - it is a small plastic part that often cracks and slips.

title: Line Voltage / Power Supply Fault

fullDescription: Error F9-v2 indicates the GE microwave has detected line voltage outside the safe operating range. Sag, surges, or a poor connection at the outlet can trigger this fault. The microwave shuts down to protect its components.

fixSteps.instruction: Use a plug-in voltage tester or multimeter to confirm the outlet reads 110-125 V AC. Anything lower indicates wiring problems.

fixSteps.title: Check the breaker and shared loads
fixSteps.instruction: Avoid running large appliances on the same circuit. Reset the breaker and try the microwave alone.

fixSteps.title: Have an electrician or technician inspect
fixSteps.instruction: If the outlet measures correctly but the code persists, the microwave's internal power supply is suspect and needs professional service.

title: Convection Element Open
shortDescription: Convection heating element electrically open.
fullDescription: On combination GE microwaves, F14 is logged when the convection element is open and a convection bake is requested.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the microwave
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave (or trip the breaker) for at least 5 minutes, then restore power. A clean reset clears transient faults caused by power glitches or stray noise on the keypad.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for visible problems
fixSteps.instruction: Open the door, remove the turntable and roller ring, and inspect the cavity, door switches, and convection element area for food debris, moisture, or obvious damage. Clean as needed and try a short test cook.

fixSteps.title: Test the convection element
fixSteps.instruction: WARNING: Microwaves contain a high-voltage capacitor that can store a lethal charge even when unplugged. Discharge the capacitor before working on internal components, or have a qualified technician do this work. With the unit unplugged and capacitor discharged, remove the outer cabinet and locate the convection element. Check connectors, harnesses, and resistance per the service manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace the faulty part

whenToCallPro: Any work involving the magnetron, high-voltage transformer, capacitor or diode should be performed by a qualified technician. The high-voltage capacitor can deliver a fatal shock even when unplugged.

faq.a: Yes.
